title: ITME: Inference Tiered Memory Expansion with Disaggregated CXL-Hybrid Memories
event_hint: Proposes CXL-hybrid tiered memory expansion to give LLM inference a TB-scale byte-addressable remote memory pool, targeting the disaggregated shared-context scaling problem.
problem: Agentic and long-context LLM workloads push context states to TB scale, beyond a single server; existing offload to DPU/JBOF via NVMe-over-fabrics still carries heavy software overhead and cost, and the ideal shared-context architecture is unsettled.
mechanism: ITME uses a CXL-hybrid memory to expose a massive TB-scale byte-addressable remote memory expansion. The key insight is that model weights and prefix caches have deterministic access patterns, so the system proactively manages data movement across the memory-storage hierarchy, simplifying the software stack via direct byte-addressability and adding remote expansion beyond host memory for large KV cache footprints.

evidence.claim: ITME achieves up to a 35.7% throughput improvement over conventional CPU-offloading.
evidence.condition: providing additional remote memory expansion to accommodate large KV cache footprints beyond host memory limits

evidence.claim: Performance validated with production-grade SK Hynix CMM and PCIe Gen5 NVMe SSDs; functional feasibility shown via an FPGA-based hardware prototype.
evidence.condition: CXL-hybrid memory + PCIe Gen5 NVMe; FPGA prototype for functional validation

evaluation_context: Evaluated with production-grade SK Hynix CXL memory modules (CMM) and PCIe Gen5 NVMe SSDs for performance, plus an FPGA-based prototype for functional feasibility. Baseline is conventional CPU-offloading for KV cache beyond host memory.
limitations: Abstract-level only; full body not fetched. The 35.7% figure is an upper bound ('up to'); exact workload sizes, model types, and the full throughput/latency curves are in the body. CXL-hybrid tiering also depends on the deterministic-access-pattern assumption holding for non-prefix-cache traffic.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to CXL/disaggregated-memory and KVCache cross-node transfer themes: it externalizes inference KV cache / prefix cache to a TB-scale CXL byte-addressable pool, directly addressing capacity limits for long-context/agentic inference. The DPU/JBOF NVMe-oF comparison also touches the DPU-offload theme as an alternative path for shared context.
